definitions.explanation: Having a rough or unrefined texture with large particles or loose weave.
Lacking precision or refinement in work or behavior.

examples.japanese: この{布|ぬの}は{目|め}が{粗|あら}い。
examples.english: This cloth has a coarse weave.

examples.japanese: {粗|あら}い{塩|しお}を{使|つか}ってください。
{仕事|しごと}が{粗|あら}いので、やり{直|なお}してください。
examples.english: Your work is sloppy, so please redo it.

notes:
{粗|あら}い is an i-adjective describing coarseness of texture or crudeness of quality.

FORMS:
- Adverbial: {粗|あら}く
- Noun form: {粗|あら}さ (coarseness)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {目|め}が{粗|あら}い (coarse weave/mesh)
- {粗|あら}い{塩|しお} (coarse salt)
- {仕事|しごと}が{粗|あら}い (sloppy work)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {粗|あら}い vs. {荒|あら}い: Both read あらい, but {粗|あら}い refers to texture/quality (coarse, crude), while {荒|あら}い refers to intensity/behavior (rough, wild, violent).

ORTHOGRAPHY:
The distinction between {粗} and {荒} is important but often confused in casual writing.
